Commentary.Commentary: We are back live with the chase. Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka are the openers for Sri Lanka while Richard Ngarava will bowl the first over.
... RUN CHASE ...

The bowlers were brilliant and they were well aided by the fielders as well. The spin duo of Maheesh Theekshana and Wanindu Hasaranga was the difference maker for the Lankans as the duo gave away just 35 runs and picked 4 wickets amongst them. Dushmantha Chameera was a bit expensive but he took a key wicket of Sikandar Raza right at the end. The target is a challenging one as the ball tends to keep low on this surface but with the Lankan Lions playing in their backyard would fancy this total. Run chase on the other side.

After being put in to bat first, Zimbabwe started their innings a bit sluggishly as they managed to score just 38 off the first 6 overs giving away a couple of wickets but a brilliant third wicket partnership of 45 runs stabled the ship for the visitors and eased them to a respectable total. Skipper Sikandar Raza was brilliant with the bat but batters around him couldn't contribute much. Sean Williams lived a charmed life but failed to make it count. Skipper Sikandar Raza was the top scorer for his side as he scored 62 off just 42 deliveries. Luke Jongwe and Brian Bennett closed the innings well with a well crafted cameo of 14 runs together.
A skipper knock from Sikandar Raza helps the visitors post a fighting total on board as Zimbabwe posts 143.
On a length much slower around off, Luke Jongwe swivels and pushes it to long leg for a single to close the innings. Zimbabwe post 143 on board.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the live-action as the umpires make their way to the middle followed by the players of Sri Lanka who position themselves to their respective field positions. Tinashe Kamunhukamwe and Craig Ervine are the openers for Zimbabwe. Angelo Mathews will start the proceedings with the ball.

Skipper of Zimbabwe, Sikandar Raza says he doesn't mind batting first. He thinks the wicket is a lot harder and the seamers and spinners will take advantage but he is not thinking about losing the toss. Adds that they know they have lost the ODI series but their whole focus is on this series.

Skipper of Sri Lanka Wanindu Hasaranga says they will bowl first as this is the first game and they are backing their bowlers. He informs that he is feeling great after the first ODI and looking to put up his best performance.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Craig Ervine, Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, Brian Bennett, Sean Williams, Sikandar Raza (C), Ryan Burl, Clive Madande (WK), Luke Jongwe, Wellington Masakadza, Blessing Muzarabani, Richard Ngarava

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Sadeera Samarawickrama, Charith Asalanka, Angelo Mathews, Wanindu Hasaranga (C), Dasun Shanaka, Maheesh Theekshana, Dushmantha Chameera, Nuwan Thushara.
TOSS -: Sri Lanka have won the coin flip and they have decided to BOWL first.

The visitors though have had problems of their own of late but they would be looking to start afresh as they have their A-side available after some time. The side does have the players that could impact any game on their day but would be looking forward to a collective performance for a longer run. The side will be led by superstar all-rounder Sikandar Raza who has a very good side consisting of Craig Ervine, Joylord Gumbie, Blessing Muzarabani, Richard Ngarava, Ryan Burl, and others. Zimbabwe were dealt a killer blow as they couldn't qualify for the 2024 T20I World Cup and would be looking to put on a performance that could help them heal those wounds to some extent. With the Lankan lions ready to roar let's see what the Zimbabweans have to offer. Stay tuned for toss and team updates.

The hosts would be looking to keep up the winning momentum from a different format as they won the ODI series against the same opposition a few days back. The side though has not been at their best recently in the T20I format but would be looking to perform better and build up to the ICC T20I World Cup tournament with victories under their belt. The side will be led by Wanindu Hasaranga. The three Lions would be delighted to have him back after a lengthy time on the sideline due to his injury. His impact was clearly to be seen in the side especially with his bowling being above par to anybody else they have. The side has a perfect blend of players who like to play on the front foot and those who can anchor an innings well. The bowling too looks solid for the hosts. Angelo Mathews will be making a comeback in the side after 3 long years.

Hello and welcome to everyone tuning in as we begin our live ball-to-ball coverage of the first of the 3-match T20I series between Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka. R. Premadasa Stadium, Colombo will be the venue for the very first game of this series.
... MATCHDAY ...

It's time to revert to the shortest format on the Sri Lankan shores after the three-match ODI series between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe. The series was marred by rain, with the first match abandoned as the rain played the spoiled sport, and the remaining two facing interruptions as well. Despite the weather challenges, the hosts clinched the series 2-0. As the T20I series approaches, both teams are hopeful for complete games without rain disruptions. The First T20I of the three-match series is scheduled at Colombo RPS, with Wanindu Hasaranga leading the stacked Sri Lankan squad. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis, consistent performers in the ODIs, alongside Kusal Perera and Sadeera Samarawickrama, will fortify the top order. The veteran Angelo Mathews returns to the pack after three years and aims to make an impact. The middle order, featuring Charith Asalanka, Dhananjaya de Silva, and Dasun Shanaka, combines experience with young talents like Kamindu Mendis. The bowling arsenal boasts Maheesh Theekshana, Matheesha Pathirana, Dushmantha Chameera, and the impressive Dilshan Madushanka, complemented by the ever-reliable Wanindu Hasaranga. Zimbabwe, who have had a pretty ordinary run since the World Cup qualifiers, will be captained by the dynamic Sikandar Raza. Batters Ryan Burl, Joylord Gumbie, and Craig Ervine, along with Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, form their lineup. Richard Ngarava and Blessing Muzarabani will be their go-to bowlers. Sri Lanka have lost their recent five fixtures, and Zimbabwe will look to spoil the hosts’ party. Premadasa Stadium of Colombo has hosted 39 T20Is so far and the teams batting second have had a slight upper hand. With top spinners in their bowling artillery, the hosts will look to exploit the sub-continental conditions, or will the tourists bounce back and surprise the hosts? Whom are you supporting?
